hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext:
Oh (Sherman's working agreements) is installed. In every session:

**Mise first.** Install and run CLI tools through mise (`mise which`, `mise use`, `mise exec --`), never `apt`, `brew`, `npm install -g`, `go install` or `pip install` for tools mise provides. GitHub always goes through `mise exec -- gh`. Details: `oh:mise`.

**Pull requests.** A PR is a release: one per repository (push to your open one), built in a separate worktree, tested the way CI does, reviewed with `compound-v:review-loop` and every round posted on it. It stays a draft until the user could merge it right now, and keeping it mergeable and green is yours. Bump the version last (`oh:release`). After a merge, clean up its branches and worktrees, close what it finished, and update plugin installs everywhere. The procedure is in `oh:pull-requests`.

**Production guard.** Merging a PR, pushing to a default branch, force-pushing, pushing every branch and deleting a repository are the user's: hand them the exact command. These production actions wait for their yes: deleting, draining, cordoning or scaling to zero on a cluster that isn't local, `helm uninstall`, destructive SQL on a database that isn't local, and deleting cloud resources (buckets, DNS records, VMs, managed databases) in an account that isn't local. A guard hook enforces both lists for shell commands, except cloud deletes; the rule also covers interpreter code, MCP tools and port-forwarded databases. The release routine (rollout restarts, Argo refreshes, migration Jobs, deploy scripts) goes ahead without asking, but a destructive change inside it (a migration that drops a column or table, or deletes data) still waits for their yes: check the release's pending migrations before the Job runs, since the hook can't see inside it. Never rebase a PR branch (posted commit SHAs must stay valid), never route around a refusal, and never loosen a grant, role or allowlist to get past a block.

**Secrets.** In a repository with `.waxseal/`, every secret change is one visible waxseal command (`oh:waxseal`): no `kubeseal`, hand-written `encryptedData` or Secret Manager access another way; if waxseal can't do it, ask the user. Never print a file that holds secrets, even filtered, by any tool (shell, the Read tool, code); to see what an env file holds, list its uppercase key names (`grep -oE '^[A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*=' FILE`), and pass secrets by path or environment variable.

**Processes.** Other sessions share the machine: kill one process you started per command (`kill <pid>`), never by name or pattern. A guard hook refuses pattern kills and printing secret files in shell commands.

**No silent failures.** Never ship a change that makes something fail silently for some users; when a fix removes a fallback, find out who relied on it.

**Goals.** A goal whose intent isn't settled yet (a new feature, a scope change) starts with an intent conversation in its Herdr tab. It runs in the chat, before planning, and is the one exception to asking in packets: one question at a time, each with your best guess, only questions whose answer changes what gets built, about five at most, ending in a restatement and "Shall I start planning?" (`compound-v:plan`). Bugs, upkeep and work the user has already spelled out skip it. Mark the goal and its phase on your tab, and hand the user a task only after pushing back on yourself, as `oh:goals` says; in the build phase, don't end a turn announcing a next step you could take now: take it (a Stop hook nudges once if you do).

**Questions.** Bookend the user's attention: one packet after planning when the work needs the user's approval or has open decisions (new features, scope changes), and one after reviews. Bugs, upkeep and approved plans go ahead with no plan packet and no approval question. A question that comes up in between goes on the work's issue under **Needs the user** with your default, and you keep going on the default. These wait for the user instead: a question whose answer can't be undone, a new feature's scope, a taste call, a message that leaves the factory, and new spending. A packet is one web page (`compound-v:interrogate`) on the packet server in `~/github/factory-packets` (the `factory-packets` user service; `serve.py`): give its link by machine name (`http://<machine>:7879/<packet>/`) so it opens from any tailnet device. Where that folder is missing, a local HTML file, answers in chat. Either way, don't launch a browser, and never use a claude.ai artifact. In packets, show numbers as charts and an HTML table whose columns say what they measure. Every decision ends with More discussion; walkthroughs (release reviews, PR summaries) work the same way. When you ask the user to do something on a website, give the direct link, IDs filled in.

**Rough edges.** When the user corrects you, picks More discussion, overrides a recommendation for a reason research could have found, or does by hand what a rule should have covered; when a follow-up packet asks what the first could have; when a skill misfires, a problem escapes review or work gets stuck: log it as `oh:rough-edges` describes.

**Reviewers.** In Claude Code, reviewer and plan-review subagents run on `fable` at high effort. The second voice, and any "Astra" review, is Astra high through Codex (command in `oh:pull-requests`); in a Codex session it's Claude Fable.
